questions.q: The client wants an AI report writer for deviations on day one. In the six-step method, when does the LLM come in?
options: First, so the client sees value in week one
Last, after process, data and systems are checked
Second, right after the first round of interviews
Never, because LLMs are not allowed in GMP work at all
questions.why: The LLM step is last. Earlier steps clean the process and data so the LLM step adds value and can be validated.

questions.q: Interviewing for a deviation process, who should you ask to walk through a recently closed deviation?
options: Operators, investigators, lab and QA reviewers
Only the site director, who sees the whole picture
Only the IT owner of the eQMS and its interfaces
Only the eQMS vendor's implementation consultant
questions.why: The people who touch each step know where time really goes and how the work differs from the SOP.

questions.q: The same event is typed into the MES, an email to QA and the eQMS. You want to remove the email step. What must happen?
options: Stop sending the emails from tomorrow morning
Ask IT to block the shared QA mailbox for everyone
Leave it, since duplicated entries are harmless
Raise a change control and update the SOP
questions.why: In GMP, a process change needs an approved SOP update through change control.

questions.q: Your SQL check shows 'human error' and 'Human Error' as two root causes. Which step of the method found this?
options: Interview the people
Map process and systems
Validate the data
Connect systems and add an LLM
questions.why: Validating the data means profiling exports for missing fields and inconsistent categories.

questions.q: In step 5 you find the eQMS audit trail is on but never reviewed. What is a sensible action?
options: Turn the audit trail off to save storage space
Ignore it, because the system is already validated
Add periodic audit trail review to the SOP
Build the AI tool now and fix the review later on
questions.why: Audit trail review is part of data integrity control, and the AI tool will rely on that trail too.

questions.q: The assistant drafts a summary and candidate root causes. Where should the draft go?
options: Straight into the approved investigation text field
Into a separate, attributed field with the record
Into a personal notes file kept by the investigator
Nowhere, it should only appear on screen and vanish
questions.why: Keeping the draft separate and attributed lets QA and inspectors see what the tool proposed and what the person decided.
